subject: Post-call: Acme integration — rate limits, retries & idempotency
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Acme integration — rate limits, retries & idempotency

Thanks for the call earlier, Liam — good to meet practically the whole infra team. Quick recap and actionable next steps from our side: 

1) What we heard (summary)
- You plan to route 2k req/s at peak for the chat endpoint (200 token average).
- Key concerns: 429s under burst, consistent latency under 200ms p50, and safe retry semantics for exactly-once user experiences.

2) Architecture follow-ups (items we said we'd provide)
- SDK setup: minimal init + sample for streaming + embeddings batch upload.
- Auth: short-lived API keys + optional mTLS for Dedicated.
- Routing: how to route dev vs prod vs fallback model variants (cost/latency tradeoffs).
- Structured output/tool calling: example schema + tool-calling best practices and fallbacks.

3) Rate limits / quotas / retries (this thread focus)
- Our recommended approach: client-side exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency tokens for mutating ops (or long-running generation jobs), and transparent 429 headers that include a retry-after and a request-id for correlation.
- We'll attach a short guide (redwood-rate-limit-guide.pdf) — includes recommended backoff parameters, server-side quotas, and sample error handling code.

4) Next steps / owners
- Aditya: share rate-limit guide + example SDK snippets (by EOD PST today).
- Acme: share a representative sample of your traffic profile and any request logs showing 429s (you mentioned a weekend spike).
- Ben / Marissa: assist with quota sizing and pilot proposal (we'll propose a Dedicated pilot if traffic pattern holds).

Attachment: redwood-rate-limit-guide.pdf (summary + sample code)

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick 30m to walk through the guide.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

Thanks Aditya — this is very helpful. Couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 2k req/s number is for our EU+US combined traffic; US alone is closer to 1.4k. Peak bursts can be 3-5x for short tails (5-10s) during product launches.
- We run a mixture of streaming and non-streaming: streaming for chat UI, non-streaming for batch reranking/embeddings jobs.
- We'll send over a 48-hour sample of logs (redacted) — attaching now: acme-rate-limit-sample-logs.txt

Questions: 
1) For idempotency tokens — is the recommended approach to include a client-generated UUID per user-interaction, or should we batch at session-level?
2) For the retry strategy you recommend, what are the default backoff windows Redwood SDKs implement (if any)?

Happy to schedule a follow-up next week after we share logs.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme integration — rate limits, retries & idempotency

Nice — thanks for the logs, Liam. Quick answers inline and a small SDK snippet below.

On idempotency tokens:
- Best practice: client-generated UUID per logical user interaction that modifies state or triggers a billable/irreversible action. For pure read/generation (stateless) you can still use tokens to dedupe when replay is possible.
- Session-level tokens are ok for aggregated batch jobs but reduce granularity for retries.

On SDK defaults (Redwood JS/Python SDKs):
- Default client retry policy (non-streaming): 5 attempts total, exponential backoff base 200ms, multiplier 2.0, capped at 10s, plus full jitter. 429 responses include a Retry-After header when appropriate.
- For streaming: we do not automatically reconnect application-level streams without developer opt-in (to avoid duplicate partial outputs). We provide helper utilities to resume using server-side continuation tokens when available.

Sample idempotent request pattern (pseudocode):

// JS SDK example
const idempotencyKey = uuidv4();
const resp = await redwood.generate({
  model: 'redwood-chat-1',
  input: userPrompt,
  idempotency_key: idempotencyKey,
});

Retry handling (recommended):
- On 429: exponential backoff with jitter; if Retry-After header present, use max(Retry-After, backoff).
- On 5xx: retry up to N (configurable), avoid retrying on 400/422.
- Include X-Request-ID: client-generated short id for correlation; server will echo.

I'll also upload a short snippet to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/acme-integration-specs (linked above).

Let us know a couple windows you have next week for a deep-dive on routing + quotas.

—
Aditya
